name: read_map
title: Read MAP.md
description: Read MAP.md — the routing table for this bundle. Call this FIRST. It is small and tells you which single file or tool answers each kind of question (who the user is, what the current tasks are, where knowledge lives, what may be written where), so you can go straight to that one place instead of reading around to find it.

name: read_human
title: Read human.md
description: Read human.md — who the user is: how to address them, how they want work done, their constraints and current context. Read this before doing substantial work for them. Creates the file from a template when it does not exist yet.

name: write_human
title: Write human.md
description: Replace human.md. Use when the user tells you something durable about themselves or how they want to be worked with. Keep it short — this file is read on every session, so length is a recurring cost.

content.description: The full new contents of human.md

name: list_tasks
title: List tasks
description: List tasks from Task.md. Returns only OPEN work (in progress, then not started) unless a status is given — the completed history is the bulk of the file and is rarely what you want. Read this to find out what to work on.

status.description: Restrict to one status: doing | todo | done. Omit for all open work.

name: daily_note
title: Open today's note
description: Get today's daily note (wiki/daily/YYYY-MM-DD.md), creating it from the template if it does not exist. Use this to record what happened today, or to read what the user wrote there.

date.description: ISO date, e.g. 2026-08-04. Defaults to today.

name: collect_daily_tasks
title: Move daily-note tasks into Task.md
description: Read today's daily note, take every UNCHECKED item under the '## タスク' heading, add each to Task.md, then tick the line and stamp it with the task id. Call this whenever you have read a daily note that contains work the user wants tracked — a requirement left in a daily note is invisible tomorrow, because Task.md is the list that gets read. Safe to call twice: ticked lines are never carried over again.

name: add_task
title: Add a task
description: Add a task to Task.md. Use when the user asks for something that will not be finished in this exchange, or when you find work that needs doing later.

title.description: What needs doing, in one line

name: update_task
title: Update a task
description: Change a task's status or fields by id (e.g. T-0007). Completing one stamps today's date. Call this when you finish something rather than leaving the list stale.

name: read_agents_md
title: Read AGENTS.md
description: Read AGENTS.md (wiki/AGENTS.md): the layer contract, the OKF frontmatter rules and the naming conventions this bundle expects. Read MAP.md first — it will tell you whether you need this.

name: open_bundle
title: Open bundle
description: Open a local directory as an OKF knowledge bundle. Not needed when the server was started with OKF_BUNDLE set.

path.description: Absolute path to the bundle root

name: bundle_info
title: Bundle info
description: Summarise the open bundle: root, wiki directory, concept count and how many concepts fail OKF conformance.

name: list_files
title: List files
description: List files and directories, annotated with the LLM Wiki layer they belong to.

path.description: Bundle-relative path; omit for the root

name: retrieve
title: Retrieve context
description: Retrieve relevant passages assembled for reasoning, with citation anchors and a character budget. This is the RAG entry point — prefer it over search when you need to ANSWER a question from the knowledge base. Returns whole sections with their heading path, not just snippets. Works with Japanese and English.

expand_neighbours.description: Include adjacent sections for continuity (default false)

path_prefix.description: Restrict to a bundle-relative path prefix

include_dead.description: Also return concepts tagged DEAD, which are left out by default (default false)

para_depth.description: Only read PARA classes up to this priority, 1-4: 1 projects, 2 +areas, 3 +resources (unfiled concepts and know-how count here), 4 everything (default)

link_depth.description: After retrieval, follow links from the returned files up to 0-2 hops and list those files' one-line descriptions (never bodies) within the same budget (default 0)

name: context_pack
title: Build a context pack
description: Assemble the MINIMAL set of files needed to start a task — relevant passages grouped by file, each file's one-line description, and the skills that match the task — within a character budget. Call this at the START of substantial work instead of reading files one by one. tier='worker' returns a small pack for a cheap or local model doing delegated work; tier='supervisor' returns a broader pack for a frontier model planning or verifying. Omit tier for a middle default. The pack also lists the best-matching know-how (lessons other agents recorded) and, with link_depth, one-line pointers to files linked from the ones above.

task.description: What the work is, in natural language

tier.description: worker | supervisor — sizes the pack to the consuming model

budget_chars.description: Character budget across all passages (overrides the tier default)

path_prefix.description: Restrict to a bundle-relative path prefix

include_dead.description: Also return concepts tagged DEAD, which are left out by default (default false)

para_depth.description: Only read PARA classes up to this priority, 1-4: 1 projects, 2 +areas, 3 +resources (unfiled concepts and know-how count here), 4 everything (default)

link_depth.description: After retrieval, follow links from the returned files up to 0-2 hops and list those files' one-line descriptions (never bodies) within the same budget (default 0)

name: search
title: Search
description: BM25 full-text search across wiki concepts, returning one hit per document. Use this to LOCATE pages (and to check whether knowledge already exists before writing). To answer a question from the content, use retrieve instead. Handles Japanese via bigram indexing. Concepts tagged DEAD are left out unless include_dead is true (to list them: tags ['DEAD'] with include_dead).

path_prefix.description: Restrict to a bundle-relative path prefix

include_dead.description: Also return concepts tagged DEAD, which are left out by default (default false)

name: list_concepts
title: List concepts
description: Every concept id with its title and type, plus its lifecycle when marked (product | dead). Use to get an overview of the bundle, or to find the exact id for a link. DEAD concepts are listed here too: this is the inventory.

name: list_tags
title: List tags and types
description: Tag and OKF type counts across the bundle, for filtering and for orientation.

name: unresolved_links
title: Unresolved links
description: Wikilinks pointing at concepts that do not exist yet. These are the knowledge gaps the bundle has already identified — good candidates for new pages.

name: read_file
title: Read file
description: Read a file relative to the bundle root. For concept documents the response also carries parsed frontmatter, outbound links and backlinks.

name: write_file
title: Write file
description: Write a file relative to the bundle root. Concept documents must carry YAML frontmatter with a non-empty 'type' (OKF v0.2); non-conformance is reported back as a warning. Writing into raw/ or .rag/ is rejected. A log.md row is appended automatically.

actor.description: Actor for the log row, e.g. process:claude-code

note.description: Optional note for the log row

name: create_concept
title: Create concept
description: Create a new OKF-conformant concept document with correct frontmatter. Prefer this over write_file for new pages — it cannot produce a non-conformant file.

type.description: OKF type, e.g. Concept, Entity, Playbook

name: backlinks
title: Backlinks
description: List concepts linking to the given concept id.

name: move_file
title: Move or rename
description: Move or rename a file within wiki/ or .rag/, rewriting every link that pointed at it (body links and the frontmatter relations entries, edited in place) so the graph stays intact; a relation it cannot edit safely is listed in the answer as dangling. Always prefer this over write_file + delete_file, which would silently break inbound links. Files in raw/ cannot be moved by an agent: promoting unreviewed material into the canonical layer is a human decision, so ask the user to do it from the UI.

name: delete_file
title: Delete
description: Delete a file. Reports which concepts had links to it, since those links become broken. Reserved files cannot be deleted.

name: create_directory
title: Create directory
description: Create a directory inside the bundle.

name: check_conformance
title: Check conformance
description: Report every document that violates OKF v0.2 §11 — missing frontmatter, missing 'type', or frontmatter on a reserved file. Schema warnings (undeclared concept types and relation kinds) are not violations and are reported by graph_schema.

name: audit_changes
title: Audit changes
description: Group log.md rows by actor to see who — the human, or which model — changed what, optionally since an ISO date. Use it to review agent-written changes before trusting them, and after several models have worked on the same bundle. Rows are returned newest first.

since.description: ISO date; only rows on or after it

actor.description: Substring filter on the actor, e.g. 'process:' for all agents

name: summarize_activity
title: Summarize activity
description: Summarize what changed in the bundle as a page you can cite: log.md rows grouped by actor, then by file, each line giving the log date and the bundle-relative path it came from, plus totals per action. Nothing is inferred beyond the log. Filter by ISO dates and an actor substring. With save: true it is also written as an ActivitySummary concept at wiki/activity/<since>_<until>[_<actor>].md (credited to 'by', or process:okf; a filter that does not survive as a file name gets a short hash appended so two filters never share a file) and the path is returned instead of the page.

since.description: ISO date; only rows on or after it

until.description: ISO date; only rows on or before it

actor.description: Substring filter on the actor, e.g. 'process:codex'. Only narrows the rows; it does not say who saves the summary.

by.description: Who is running this, e.g. 'process:claude-code'; credits a saved summary (default process:okf)

save.description: Write the summary into wiki/activity/ and return its path (default false)

name: rebuild_index
title: Rebuild index.md
description: Regenerate index.md from all concepts currently on disk.

name: rebuild_rag
title: Rebuild search index
description: Rebuild the .rag FTS5 index from scratch.

name: skill_find
title: Find a skill
description: Find which skill fits a task. CHEAP — ranks locally and returns only names, descriptions and scores, never a procedure body. Call this FIRST whenever a task might have an established procedure, then call skill_open on the winner. If confidence is 'low', compare the returned descriptions before opening one.

task.description: What the user is trying to do, in their own words.

name: skill_list
title: List skills
description: List every skill: name, description, tags, and the token cost of opening each. CHEAP — no procedure bodies. Prefer skill_find when you have a specific task; use this to see what the bundle can do.

name: skill_open
title: Open a skill
description: Load a skill's full procedure. COSTS TOKENS — call it once, for the one skill you actually need, after skill_find. Returns the body plus the names of any supporting files, which you then read individually with skill_read.

name.description: Skill name from skill_find or skill_list.

name: skill_read
title: Read a skill resource
description: Read one supporting file from inside a skill folder. Only call this for a file the opened skill actually pointed you at — reading them speculatively defeats the purpose of keeping them out of the body.

path.description: Resource path, relative to the skill folder.

name: set_para
title: Refile under PARA
description: Move a concept into one of the four PARA folders: project (in progress, has an end), area (no deadline but deliberately prioritised), resource (useful knowledge), archive (not in use). This is a real move, so links are rewritten. Use archive rather than delete when something stops being current — archived notes stay findable but rank far below everything else.

name: list_para
title: List by PARA
description: Every concept grouped by PARA class, in priority order. Use it to see what is actually active before deciding what to work on, or to find stale notes that belong in the archive.

para.description: Restrict to one class. Omit for all.

name: set_lifecycle
title: Mark Product or DEAD
description: Mark a concept's lifecycle with a frontmatter tag: 'product' (a finished, trusted result - ranks slightly higher), 'dead' (retired - left out of search, retrieve and context_pack unless include_dead is true; NOT deleted, links and history stay), or 'none' to clear. A concept is never both. To list retired files: search with tags ['DEAD'] and include_dead true.

actor.description: Who is making the change, e.g. process:claude-code.

name: knowhow_find
title: Find know-how
description: Find lessons other agents recorded that fit a task: pitfalls, conventions, 'this worked'. CHEAP — returns titles, descriptions, scores and who recorded each, never the body (read_file the ones that apply). Call this before starting work; context_pack already includes the top three.

task.description: What you are about to do, in natural language.

name: knowhow_add
title: Record know-how
description: Record one short lesson for the agents that come after you, after a non-obvious discovery: a pitfall, a convention, something that worked. One lesson per call, written so it makes sense without this conversation. Stored in wiki/knowhow/ with who recorded it. Lighter than a skill — if it is a full procedure, write a skill instead.

title.description: The lesson in a few words.

body.description: What happened and what to do about it. Start with the one-line takeaway.

actor.description: Which agent is recording this, e.g. process:claude-code or process:codex.

name: base_list
title: List bases
description: List the .base files in wiki/ with the views each offers (name and type). A base is a saved list or aggregate over the concepts - for example 'every Product by PARA, with counts'. Check here before scanning many files to answer a list or count question: if a base already answers it, base_query returns the rows directly.

name: base_query
title: Query a base
description: Run one view of a .base file over the concepts and return JSON (columns, rows or groups, summaries, warnings) plus a compact Markdown table in 'markdown'. Rows are ordered deterministically and capped at 500. Use this instead of reading many files for lists, counts and aggregates (e.g. all Product concepts per PARA class). Supports table and cards views; formulas, sorting, grouping and summaries are evaluated for you.

path.description: Bundle-relative path of the .base file, e.g. wiki/bases/products-and-dead.base.

view.description: View name (see base_list). Defaults to the first view.

limit.description: Return at most this many rows (a positive integer; the view's own limit still applies).

name: base_write
title: Write a base
description: Create or replace a .base file under wiki/. The YAML and the supported subset are checked first and nothing is written if they are invalid; the text is saved exactly as given, so keys this app does not use survive. Format (Obsidian Bases): top-level filters (a string expression, or and/or/not lists), formulas, properties (displayName), summaries, and views of type table or cards with name, filters, order, sort ([{property, direction}]), limit, groupBy ({property, direction}) and summaries ({property: Sum}). File properties: file.name, basename, path, folder, ext, mtime, tags, links, properties, plus file.para; file.hasTag(), file.inFolder(), file.hasLink() work. Frontmatter keys are bare names or note.NAME; formulas are formula.NAME. Create a base when you expect to ask the same list or count question again.

path.description: Bundle-relative path ending in .base, under wiki/, e.g. wiki/bases/open-projects.base.

content.description: The full YAML text of the base.

name: canvas_list
title: List canvases
description: List the .canvas files under wiki/ (JSON Canvas 1.0, as Obsidian reads it) with their node and edge counts. A canvas is a relationship diagram: file nodes pointing at concepts, text, link and group nodes, and edges between them. Check here before drawing a new one.

name: canvas_read
title: Read a canvas
description: Read one .canvas file as structured JSON ('canvas': nodes and edges exactly as stored) plus a compact text 'outline': nodes by group with file nodes resolved to the concept's title and description, then the edges with their labels. Read the outline to understand a diagram without rendering it.

path.description: Bundle-relative path of the .canvas file, e.g. wiki/graph/canvases/overview.canvas.

name: canvas_write
title: Write a canvas
description: Create or replace a .canvas file under wiki/ (not in a hidden folder). The JSON is checked against the JSON Canvas 1.0 spec first (node types text, file, link and group; integer x, y, width and height; edges between existing node ids; sides top/right/bottom/left; ends none/arrow; colours '1'-'6' or #hex) and within bounds (1 MiB, 2000 nodes, 5000 edges, 32 levels deep); nothing is written if it is invalid. The text is saved exactly as given, so unknown keys and the order of nodes and edges survive a round trip with Obsidian. A file node's 'file' is a bundle-relative path such as wiki/3-resources/foo.md.

path.description: Bundle-relative path ending in .canvas, under wiki/, e.g. wiki/graph/canvases/overview.canvas.

content.description: The full JSON text of the canvas.

name: canvas_from_links
title: Draw concept relationships
description: Draw the neighbourhood of a concept (root) or of what a retrieval query finds (query, its top 5 hits) as a canvas, following wiki links, Markdown links and typed relations in both directions up to depth steps (0-3, default 1), and save it. Layout is deterministic: a column per distance from the root, concepts ordered by path, fixed sizes; plain links are unlabeled, typed relations carry their kind; roots are green, DEAD concepts red. Links to missing concepts and self-links are not drawn. At most 150 concepts and 5000 edges are drawn. Refuses to replace an existing canvas unless overwrite is true. Returns where it was saved and the text outline.

root.description: The concept to centre on: its id (topics/foo), its path (wiki/topics/foo.md) or a unique bare name.

query.description: Instead of (or as well as) root: a search query whose best hits are the centre.

depth.description: How many link steps out to follow, 0-3 (default 1).

include_dead.description: Also return concepts tagged DEAD, which are left out by default (default false)

para_depth.description: Only read PARA classes up to this priority, 1-4: 1 projects, 2 +areas, 3 +resources (unfiled concepts and know-how count here), 4 everything (default)

group_by_para.description: Frame concepts of the same PARA class in each column with a group node (default false).

path.description: Where to save, ending in .canvas (under wiki/). A bare file name goes in wiki/graph/canvases/.

overwrite.description: Replace a canvas that already exists at path (default false: refuse, so a hand-made canvas is not lost).

name: graph_schema
title: Read the graph schema
description: Read wiki/graph/schema.md parsed: the concept 'types' and relation 'kinds' (name, description, optional from/to types) this bundle declares. Concepts declare typed relations in their frontmatter as relations: {kind: [path or [[link]], ...]}; its 'warnings' lists concept types and relation kinds not declared here (never violations). If 'exists' is false the bundle has no schema and nothing is checked.

name: system_map
title: Read SYSTEMMAP.md
description: Read SYSTEMMAP.md, the map of the system itself: layers, folders, tool groups, where bases, canvases, skills, loops, know-how and the graph live, and how to extend each. Between its markers is an auto-generated section with the current counts and listings (concepts per PARA and type, bases, canvases, skills, loops, know-how, schema types and kinds, tool count). With refresh true, that section alone is regenerated and saved (text outside the markers is never touched; a bundle without the file gets it). Refresh after adding types, relation kinds, bases, canvases, skills or loops.

refresh.description: Regenerate and save the auto-generated section (default false: just read).

name: loop_define
title: Define a loop
description: Create or update a loop design — a repeatable unit of work such as 'ingest meeting notes' or 'weekly lint'. One design is one file under loops/, and every run of it appends to that same file. Updating a design never rewrites its run history.

goal.description: What this loop accomplishes, every time it runs.

name.description: Loop name (lowercase, digits, hyphens). Derived from the goal if omitted.

skill.description: Skill to follow on each run.

checks.description: What must be true before a run is finished. Returned again by loop_end.

name: loop_start
title: Start a run
description: BEGIN HERE for any task that will change the bundle. Starts a run of an existing loop design: snapshots the bundle, returns the design's skill and completion checks, and tells you how the last run went. Only one run may be in progress at a time — close the previous one with loop_end first. Pass a goal to define the loop on the spot when it does not exist yet.

goal.description: Used to create the design if it does not exist yet.

name: loop_note
title: Note a step
description: Append a line to the running run's journal. File writes, moves and deletes are journalled automatically — use this for decisions and findings that leave no other trace, e.g. why an approach was rejected.

name: loop_end
title: End the run
description: FINISH HERE. Snapshots the bundle again, reports what changed against the preflight, and closes the run in its design's file. Returns the design's completion checks so they can be confirmed. Flags a rise in OKF non-conformance as a regression — fix it rather than leaving the run closed on a worse bundle.

outcome.description: What was accomplished, and what is left.

status.description: 'done' (default) or 'abandoned' when the work was not completed.

name: loop_list
title: List loops
description: Every loop design with its goal, skill, run count and how the last run went. Also reports which run is in progress, if any. Call this when resuming work.

name: loop_read
title: Read a loop
description: One loop design in full: its goal, completion checks, and run history. Use it to see how this work went before.
